sentences.text: Octopuses have blue blood. No, they're not secretly ocean royalty. Their blood chemistry really is different from ours.
Human blood carries oxygen using hemoglobin, a protein containing iron. It's what makes our blood red.
Octopuses use a different oxygen-carrying protein, called hemocyanin. It contains copper, and gives their blood its blue color.
Same basic job: pick up oxygen, carry it around the body, and help power the muscles. Different protein, different metal.
And their circulation has another surprise. An octopus has three hearts, not one.
Two hearts pump blood through the gills to pick up oxygen. The third sends that oxygen-rich blood around the body.
So, three hearts and blue blood... is an octopus an overachiever, or just very committed to premium plumbing?
